decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) a correlated abrupt drop in N and U near index 475–480 without clear recovery, and (2) a coherent multi-axis linear trend beginning at index 725 and continuing to 729, distinct from prior variability. Other intervals show typical GNSS noise or smooth motion without compelling morphological anomalies.

regions.observation: Cross-axis shape shows a multi-sample drop in N and U around index 475–480, with E showing a shallower, delayed dip; the N and U drops appear abrupt and possibly correlated, lacking clear immediate return within the window—suggests a candidate offset or transient motion.

From ~725 onward, all three axes (N/E/U) exhibit a coherent, sustained linear trend over just 5 samples: N declines steadily, E flattens then dips, U drops sharply—this is atypical compared to earlier noise-dominated behavior and may indicate a platform shift or data artifact; the abrupt onset at 725 and monotonic evolution through 729 warrants inspection.
